title: Model profile release oracle and staged republish procedure
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Background: As we onboard more open models and publish Redwood-verified performance profiles, operational friction arises when a published profile is discovered to be inaccurate (regression in latency or cost) or incompatible with a new runtime kernel. Current publish/rollback flows are manual, slow, and risk customer-facing instability.

Objective: Define and build an automated 'release oracle' and an associated staged republish procedure that reduces mean time to corrective action for published profile regressions, minimizes blast radius, and provides clear deterministic criteria for automated rollback and hotfix republishing. The solution should combine verification checks, sampled shadow traffic, and a fast rollback path.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-managed runbook, acceptance criteria, rollout phases, telemetry, and stakeholder alignment. Implementation details will be tracked in ENG follow-ups (ENG-21933 for verification harness, ENG-23010 for publish API changes). Not in scope: major runtime kernel changes and billing model adjustments.

Context & motivation: We observed three incidents in the last six months where a published performance profile underestimated 95th percentile latency under real traffic patterns after a runtime change. Resolution required manual rollback and cross-team coordination ~6-12 hours per incident. Automated detection and a staged republish flow will cut that to under 60 minutes for standard cases and provide predictable steps for complex ones.
acceptance_criteria: A release oracle exists that runs a verification suite against candidate profile publishes and returns PASS/FAIL with a deterministic reason code
Staged republish flow is documented and automated for the common path: validate -> staged publish -> shadow sampling -> gradual promotion
Rollback automation can be triggered within the console and via API and completes profile reversion within 15 minutes for standard cases
Telemetry shows a sampled shadow traffic pipeline that compares P50/P95 latency and cost per-token between current and candidate profile for at least 1% of live requests
On-call runbooks updated with playbook steps and a postmortem template linked to profile publishes
tasks: Define deterministic verification checks for latency, throughput, and cost deltas (PM lead)
Agree on threshold gates (e.g., P95 latency +20% or cost +15% triggers FAIL) (PM + Eng)
Design the staged publish API: candidate profiles, stage window, sampling percentage, auto-promote rules (Eng - ENG-23010)
Implement release oracle that executes verification and emits reason codes (Eng - ENG-21933)
Build console UI affordances for staged republish and one-click rollback (Design + Eng)
Create telemetry dashboard and alerts comparing candidate vs baseline across regions (Observability)
Draft runbook and add to operations playbook library (PM)
Run a dry-run with non-production models and report findings (PM + Eng)
Pilot staged republish on 2 low-risk models (one short-context, one long-context) and collect metrics
Update docs: onboarding guide, publish checklist, and FAQ (Docs)
Conduct tabletop runbook exercise with on-call and support (PM)
Coordinate security review for publish automation and sampling pipelines
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (design): finalize verification checks and thresholds - 2 weeks
Phase 1 (internal dry-run): release oracle v1 against staging models and iterate - 1 week
Phase 2 (pilot): staged republish on two low-risk models with 1% shadow sampling - 2 weeks
Phase 3 (measured rollout): widen pilot to 10 models, enable auto-promote for PASS candidates - 2 weeks
Phase 4 (GA): enable in console for all verified-profile publishers, deprecate manual-only flows - gated by security review and GA checklist
telemetry_and_alerts: Realtime comparison metric: candidate_vs_baseline.P95_latency (alert if > +20% over 5m)
Cost delta per 1k tokens (alert if > +15% over 1h)
Shadow mismatch rate (fraction of requests with significant output-level divergence) - dashboard only
Publish-failure reason codes tracked and surfaced in console
Audit log entry for every staged publish, promote, and rollback (retain 365 days)
risks: Shadow sampling adds overhead to runtime; need to ensure sampling path is efficient and does not inflate costs
False positives from verification checks could block legitimate publishes; thresholds must be empirically validated
Permissions model for automated rollback must be tightly controlled to avoid accidental mass rollbacks
Customers on Dedicated/Private may require a different opt-in model for automated sampling due to network policies
open_questions: What exact sampling % is acceptable for GA across Hosted vs Dedicated environments?
Should we permit auto-promote (zero-touch) for PASS candidates or require manual confirm for the first 24 hours?
How do we surface nuanced performance regressions that only appear under long sequences ( > 2048 tokens)?
What RBAC roles can trigger automated rollback; do we need an approval flow for >X% traffic impact?
